title: One-Week Low-Sodium Meal Plan
summary: This week's plan focuses on fresh, whole foods to support weight management and reduce sodium intake. Meals are flavored with herbs, spices, and citrus instead of salt, and a daily movement guide helps increase physical activity.

recipes.title: Quinoa Salad with Chickpeas and Bell Pepper
ingredients: 100 g chickpeas, no salt added, rinsed
steps: Place the simmering basket into the mixing bowl. Weigh 75 g quinoa into it and add 150 g water to the bowl.
Cook 15 min/100°C/speed 4.
Remove the simmering basket with the spatula and let the quinoa cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, 100 g chickpeas, diced bell pepper, and 50 g baby spinach.
Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and season with black pepper. Mix well before serving.
recipes.why: This dish is made with whole-grain quinoa and vegetables, and is flavored with lemon and pepper instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: Reducing sodium intake is one of the most cost-effective measures to improve health and reduce the burden of noncommunicable diseases. [WHO — Sodium reduction (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Steamed Salmon with Broccoli and Lemon
steps: Add 500 g water to the mixing bowl.
Place 300 g broccoli florets into the Varoma dish. Season 300 g salmon fillets with 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 g herbs, 1 g pepper, and juice from half a lemon. Place fillets on the Varoma tray.
Assemble the Varoma and secure the lid.
Cook in Steaming mode 20 min/speed 2.
Serve one portion immediately with a wedge of the remaining lemon. Let the other portion cool and store for lunch.
recipes.why: This meal includes fish and vegetables, with no added salt, using lemon and herbs for flavor.
recipes.evidence: For adults, WHO recommends less than 2000 mg/day of sodium (equivalent to less than 5 g/day salt), or just under a teaspoon. [WHO — Sodium reduction (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Steamed Salmon with Broccoli and Lemon
ingredients: 1 serving leftover Steamed Salmon with Broccoli and Lemon
steps: Enjoy the leftover salmon and broccoli cold, or gently reheat in a microwave.
Squeeze fresh lemon over the top if desired before serving.
recipes.why: This meal includes fish and vegetables, with no added salt, using lemon and herbs for flavor.
recipes.evidence: Unsaturated fat (found in fish, avocado and nuts, and in sunflower, soybean, canola and olive oils) is preferable to saturated fat. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Herbed Chicken and Vegetable Stir-fry with Brown Rice
ingredients: 150 g chicken breast, cut into strips
steps: Place simmering basket in mixing bowl, add 75 g brown rice and 800 g water. Cook 25 min/100°C/speed 4. Set rice aside and empty bowl.
Place 1 garlic clove in bowl, chop 3 sec/speed 5. Scrape down.
Add 10 g olive oil and 150 g chicken strips. Sauté 5 min/120°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Add 100 g zucchini and 100 g bell peppers. Cook 7 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Season with 2 g mixed herbs and 1 g black pepper. Stir 10 sec/Reverse/speed 2.
Serve the chicken and vegetables over the cooked brown rice.
recipes.why: No added salt: this dish uses garlic and herbs for flavor, served with whole-grain rice and lean protein.
recipes.evidence: On average, carbohydrates in the diet should come primarily from whole grains, vegetables, fruits, and pulses (like beans, lentils, and chickpeas). [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Turkey and Avocado Sandwich
ingredients: 75 g turkey breast slices, low sodium
steps: Toast 2 slices of whole-grain bread if desired.
Mash 1/4 avocado with 1 tsp lemon juice and spread on one slice of bread.
Layer with 75 g low-sodium turkey slices and a handful of baby spinach.
Top with the second slice of bread and serve.
recipes.why: A simple lunch with lean protein, whole grains, and healthy fats from avocado, using low-sodium ingredients.

recipes.title: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Soup
steps: Place onion, garlic, carrot, and zucchini into mixing bowl. Chop 5 sec/speed 5.
Scrape down sides. Add 20 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 150 g rinsed lentils, 600 g low-sodium vegetable stock, 2 g herbs, and 1 g pepper.
Cook 30 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve one portion hot. Allow the other portion to cool before storing for lunch.
recipes.why: This soup is packed with vegetables and plant-based protein from lentils, using low-sodium stock and no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Eating at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day is part of a healthy diet. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Soup
ingredients: 1 serving leftover Lentil and Vegetable Soup
steps: Reheat the leftover soup in the Thermomix for 5 min/90°C/speed 1, or in a saucepan on the stove or in a microwave.
Serve hot.
recipes.why: This soup is packed with vegetables and plant-based protein from lentils, using low-sodium stock and no added salt.
recipes.evidence: To lose weight, you need to take in fewer calories than you use up. [MedlinePlus — Weight control]

recipes.title: Steamed Cod with Cherry Tomatoes and Zucchini
steps: Add 500 g water to the mixing bowl.
On a piece of baking paper, place 150 g cod fillet. Top with 100 g zucchini, 100 g cherry tomatoes, and sliced garlic. Drizzle with 10 g olive oil and season with 1 g pepper.
Fold the baking paper into a parcel and place it on the Varoma tray.
Assemble the Varoma and secure the lid.
Cook in Steaming mode 20 min/speed 2.
Carefully open the parcel and serve immediately.
recipes.why: A light, low-sodium meal featuring lean fish and vegetables, steamed to retain nutrients.

recipes.title: Spinach Salad with Hard-Boiled Egg and Walnuts
steps: Place 500 g water and 1 egg into the mixing bowl.
Cook 14 min/100°C/speed 1 for a hard-boiled egg.
Remove the egg and place it in cold water to cool before peeling and slicing.
In a bowl, combine 100 g baby spinach, 15 g walnuts, and sliced apple.
Top with the sliced hard-boiled egg.
Whisk together 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar and 1 tsp olive oil for the dressing and pour over the salad.
recipes.why: This salad provides protein, healthy fats from walnuts, and plenty of greens, with a simple, salt-free dressing.
recipes.evidence: Protein can come from a mix of animal and plant sources. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Herb-Spiced Tofu Stew with Brown Rice
steps: Place simmering basket in mixing bowl, add 150 g brown rice and 800 g water. Cook 25 min/100°C/speed 4. Set rice aside and empty bowl.
Place onion and garlic in bowl, chop 5 sec/speed 5. Scrape down.
Add 15 g olive oil and bell pepper, sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 300 g tofu, 400 g stock, 5 g herbs, and 1 g pepper.
Cook 15 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve half the stew with half the rice. Cool and store the remaining portions for lunch.
recipes.why: A plant-based meal with protein from tofu, whole-grain rice, and vegetables, seasoned with herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: Americans consume too much sodium, on average over 3,100 milligrams per day. [American Heart Association — How much sodium should I eat per day?]

recipes.title: Herb-Spiced Tofu Stew with Brown Rice
ingredients: 1 serving leftover Tofu Stew and Brown Rice
steps: Reheat the leftover tofu stew and rice in a microwave or on the stovetop until hot.
Serve immediately.
recipes.why: A plant-based meal with protein from tofu, whole-grain rice, and vegetables, seasoned with herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: For most people, reducing sodium intake by 1,000 mg a day can improve blood pressure. [American Heart Association — How much sodium should I eat per day?]

recipes.title: Steamed Chicken Breast with Quinoa and Carrots
steps: Add 500 g water to the mixing bowl. Insert the simmering basket and weigh in 75 g quinoa.
Place 150 g sliced carrots into the Varoma dish.
Season 150 g chicken breast with olive oil, pepper, and herbs, then place on the Varoma tray.
Assemble the Varoma and cook in Steaming mode 25 min/speed 2.
Check that chicken is cooked through. Serve the chicken, quinoa, and carrots together.
recipes.why: A balanced meal with lean protein, whole grains, and vegetables, cooked without added salt.
recipes.evidence: A healthy lifestyle, including healthy eating patterns and regular physical activity, can help you lose weight. [MedlinePlus — Weight control]

recipes.title: Ricotta on Whole-Grain Toast with Sliced Apple
steps: Toast 2 slices of whole-grain bread.
Spread 100 g of ricotta cheese evenly over the toast.
Arrange the sliced apple on top of the ricotta.
Sprinkle with a little black pepper and serve.
recipes.why: This simple lunch combines protein from ricotta with fiber from whole-grain bread and fruit.
recipes.evidence: Eating more nutrient-rich foods, such as foods with lots of vitamins, minerals, and fiber, can help with weight control. [MedlinePlus — Weight control]

recipes.title: Whole-Wheat Pasta with Cannellini Bean and Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 100 g cannellini beans, no salt added, rinsed
steps: Cook 75 g of whole-wheat pasta according to package directions on the stovetop. Drain and set aside.
Place garlic and onion in the mixing bowl, chop 5 sec/speed 5.
Add 10 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 150 g cherry tomatoes, 100 g cannellini beans, 50 g water, and 2 g herbs.
Cook 10 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Pour the sauce over the cooked pasta and serve immediately.
recipes.why: This dish features whole-wheat pasta with a vegetable and bean sauce, providing fiber and plant-based protein with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: On average, overweight and obesity tend to run in families, which suggests that genes may play a role in weight gain. [MedlinePlus — Weight control]

movement: Mon: 30-minute brisk walk during your lunch break.
Tue: Take the stairs whenever possible. Do 2 sets of 10 bodyweight squats.
Wed: 45-minute brisk walk in a park or your neighborhood.
Thu: 20-minute morning walk. In the evening, do 2 sets of 10 push-ups (on knees if needed) and 2 sets of a 20-second plank.
Fri: Aim for a 30-minute brisk walk at any point in the day.
Sat: Enjoy a longer 60-minute walk, perhaps exploring a new route.
Sun: A relaxing 20-minute walk and some gentle stretching.
